rules.title: Jersey City ban on rent-setting algorithms (RealPage-type software)
rules.requirement: The City Council passed an ordinance banning landlords' use of rent-setting algorithms such as RealPage, including software that uses certain nonpublic data to set rents. The article gives no detailed operative text.
rules.coverage_text: Landlords/rental owners using rent-setting algorithms in Jersey City; article does not state unit-count or building-age limits.
rules.exemptions_text: Real estate agents were reportedly excluded at the sponsor's agreement; commenters discuss whether Multiple Listing Services are excluded; owners of multiple buildings using algorithms but not colluding were described as not covered.

exemption_tests.description: Real estate agents/realtors reportedly excluded from the ordinance.

rules.citation: Jersey City Council ordinance banning rent-setting algorithms (approved 9-0, May 21, 2025; no ordinance number given)
rules.quoted_span: The Jersey City Council unanimously approved (9-0) a measure banning rent-setting algorithms such as RealPage, as well as increasing benefits for laborers, at last night’s meeting.
rules.penalty: A commenter referred to a $2,000 daily fine; the article does not confirm the penalty in the ordinance text.
rules.ambiguity_note: News article only; effective date, ordinance number, mayoral signature and final text not stated. Status assumed in force after council passage. Amendments may still occur.
